recommendations.title: Avenues for prevention using the epidemiology of sport-related concussion from a large high school surveillance study.
recommendations.authors: Abigail C. Bretzin; Alyssa M. Pollard-McGrandy; E. Reid Davis; Douglas J. Wiebe; Tracey Covassin
recommendations.reason: The statewide, season-long surveillance contains separable high-school soccer concussion findings and a mappable clinical definition, but it calculates incidence only from athletic participant counts per 100 player-seasons. It reports no time exposure, athlete-exposures, match-exposures, valid published time rate, or defensible derivation inputs.
recommendations.studyDesign: Retrospective cohort analysis of eight years of mandated statewide head-injury surveillance.
recommendations.dataCollectionTiming: Schools submitted head-injury reports during MHSAA-sponsored practices and competitions from 2015/2016 through 2022/2023; the paper retrospectively analysed those surveillance records.
recommendations.populationEligibility: Competitive high-school student-athletes, with boys' and girls' association-football (soccer) results reported separately from other sports.
recommendations.competitionContext: Michigan High School Athletic Association sanctioned in-season practices, scrimmages, and games.
recommendations.dataSource: MHSAA Head Injury Reporting System, populated by identified athletic trainers, coaches, or administrators; confirmed concussions required diagnosis by an MD, DO, PA, or NP.
recommendations.outcomeEligibility: Confirmed sport-related concussion counts and sport-specific frequencies are eligible health outcomes, including a separable soccer subgroup.
recommendations.injuryIllnessDefinition: MHSAA defined SRC as a head injury in a sanctioned in-season event with signs, symptoms, or behaviours consistent with concussion, requiring removal and medical diagnosis.
recommendations.reportedDenominator: Athletic participant counts expressed as clinical incidence per 100 player-seasons, not a permitted exposure denominator.
recommendations.denominatorEvidenceQuote: We calculated the clinical incidence of SRC, dividing the number of SRCs by the number of athletic participants multiplied by 100 player-seasons.
evidenceQuotes: Beginning in the 2015/2016 season, the Michigan High School Athletic Association (MHSAA) requires all high schools to report all head injuries incurred during an MHSAA-sponsored practice or competition into their Head Injury Reporting System (HIRS).
MHSAA defines an SRC as a head injury resulting from a sanctioned in-season practice, scrimmage, or game.
We calculated the clinical incidence of SRC, dividing the number of SRCs by the number of athletic participants multiplied by 100 player-seasons.
sourceLocations: S925.pdf p. 2, Methods, Operational Definition of SRC

recommendations.title: Injuries in athletic club players: growth and maturation as potential risk factors (PhD Academy Award).
recommendations.reason: This two-page BJSM PhD Academy Award item is an editorial-style thesis summary, not a report of one primary study or a declared eligible systematic review. It describes a thesis and cites the underlying articles rather than supplying a study-specific methods-and-results report for extraction.
recommendations.studyDesign: PhD Academy Award editorial/thesis summary; no single primary-study design is reported as the publication's own design.
recommendations.dataCollectionTiming: The item narratively summarises thesis work spanning Athletic Club monitoring from 1997 to 2022, without reporting a standalone study protocol or results dataset.
recommendations.populationEligibility: The summary concerns Athletic Club male academy association-football players, but it is not itself an eligible primary-study report.
recommendations.competitionContext: Athletic Club academy and professional Spanish La Liga environment, described at thesis level.
recommendations.dataSource: Narrative summary of routine club monitoring and cited thesis papers, not a report of a discrete study dataset in this publication.
recommendations.outcomeEligibility: Injury epidemiology is described narratively, but the publication itself is not an eligible empirical report.
recommendations.injuryIllnessDefinition: The summary refers to the International Federation of Association Football consensus, but does not supply a standalone primary-study case definition and results.
recommendations.reportedDenominator: No study-specific numeric exposure, athlete-exposure, match-exposure, or rate is reported in this award-summary publication.
recommendations.denominatorEvidenceQuote: Individual exposure was recorded since the season of 2011–2012, which allowed us to describe injury incidence (number of injuries/exposure) and injury burden (number of days lost/exposure) for each injury in each category.
recommendations.denominatorSourceLocation: S1148.pdf p. 1, HOW DID I DO IT?
evidenceQuotes: The main aims of this thesis were to describe the epidemiology of adolescent footballers, to describe how growth and maturation are associated with injury risk in academy male players and to study the accuracy of methods to estimate somatic maturity status.
This thesis analysed injury, anthropometric and skeletal age data from routine monitoring of players at Athletic Club.

recommendations.title: Adductor-related groin injury: Prevalence and etiology during NCAA football games on artificial and natural grass surfaces.
recommendations.authors: Jarrett L. Mitton; Michael C. Meyers; Irene van Woerden; Ryan P. Lindsay; James C. Sterling; Shad K. Robinson
recommendations.reason: Despite the word 'football' in the title, the cohort is NCAA Football Bowl Subdivision American football. The paper's comparison with soccer occurs only in the Introduction and does not supply a separable association-football dataset.
recommendations.dataCollectionTiming: Athletic trainers prospectively recorded game-related injuries over 16 competitive seasons, 2006 to 2021.
recommendations.populationEligibility: Collegiate American-football athletes from 41 NCAA Football Bowl Subdivision universities, not an eligible FIFA football population.
recommendations.competitionContext: NCAA Football Bowl Subdivision university games on artificial and natural grass.
recommendations.dataSource: Certified athletic trainers' injury-surveillance forms with physician follow-up where necessary.
recommendations.outcomeEligibility: Adductor-related groin injury surveillance, but exclusively in American football.
recommendations.injuryIllnessDefinition: A reportable injury was game-related football trauma reported or treated by an athletic trainer or physician that caused absence from all or part of a game.
recommendations.reportedDenominator: 2,243 NCAA American-football games, with injury rates per 10 games.
recommendations.denominatorEvidenceQuote: Of the 2243 games documented, 1061 (47.3%) were played on artificial turf and 1182 games (52.7%) on natural grass.
evidenceQuotes: Objective: To quantify the incidence and etiology of groin trauma during college football games across artificial and natural grass surfaces.
Participants: Athletic trainers from 41 Football Bowl Subdivision universities evaluated injuries sustained by collegiate football athletes.

Therefore, based on (1) the excessive physical demands placed on the body by American football ... the purpose of this study will be to quantify the long-term prevalence and etiology of groin injuries during game-related National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) football competition.
recommendations.auditNotes: Readable 11-page English full text with no packet extraction warnings. The occurrence of 'soccer' is background/reference discussion only. PDF SHA-256 matches retrieval-manifest.json. Local recommendation only.

recommendations.title: ACL Denmark: A nationwide register-questionnaire study from 2000 to 2018 reporting stable ACL incidence rates but rising rates of reconstruction.
recommendations.authors: Niels Christian Kaldau; Kristoffer Weisskirchner Barfod; Matilde Winther-Jensen; Per Hølmich
recommendations.exclusionReason: Ineligible register, hospital, database, or public source
recommendations.reason: The source is the Danish National Patient Registry, supplemented by a retrospective questionnaire of registered patients and population/athlete registry figures. It does not report prospectively collected injury outcomes from current participating football teams or their clinical staff. Its sport-specific metric is per 100,000 registered athletes, not an eligible exposure denominator.
recommendations.dataCollectionTiming: The study retrospectively identified 2000 to 2018 patient-register records and invited surviving registry patients to a questionnaire in December 2021.
recommendations.populationEligibility: Mixed adult Danish ACL patients across sports; football is a reported injury activity but the paper does not use a football-team surveillance cohort.
recommendations.footballDiscipline: Association football occurs as a self-reported sport-at-injury category within a mixed-sport national patient cohort.
recommendations.competitionContext: Nationwide Danish health-system and sport-registration data, not a football competition surveillance setting.
recommendations.dataSource: Danish National Patient Registry, Civil Registration System, Danish sport-organisation athlete registers, and a questionnaire sent to registry patients.
recommendations.outcomeEligibility: ACL ruptures are health outcomes, but ascertainment is national patient-register and questionnaire based rather than current football-participant surveillance.
recommendations.injuryIllnessDefinition: ACL/other cruciate injury classification is based on patient-register diagnostic codes corrected with patient self-report, not a football surveillance definition.
recommendations.reportedDenominator: Annual Danish population counts and registered-athlete counts, reported as injuries per 100,000 inhabitants or athletes, without time, athlete-exposure, match-exposure, or valid derivation inputs.
recommendations.denominatorEvidenceQuote: Sports-specific ACL IRs (2012–2018) were estimated by combining self-reported injury data with sports participation figures from the National Olympic Committee and Sports Confederation of Denmark.
evidenceQuotes: This was a registry study from the DNPR with prospectively collected data on the cohort of interest.
The registry cohort (R-cohort) with all patients identified in the DNPR.
The Danish National Patient Register (DNPR) registers all patients with a diagnosis of ACL rupture.

recommendations.studyDesign: PhD Academy Award editorial/thesis summary; no single primary-study design is reported as the publication's own design.

recommendations.populationEligibility: Youth male association-football players are described, but this award-summary item is not itself an eligible primary-study report.
recommendations.competitionContext: Kosovo youth football, U15, U17, and U19, described as an underlying thesis-study context.
recommendations.dataSource: Narrative summary of four thesis articles and their underlying studies, not a discrete empirical report in this publication.

recommendations.injuryIllnessDefinition: The item refers to time-loss injuries in underlying work but does not give a standalone primary-study definition and dataset.
recommendations.reportedDenominator: No study-specific numeric exposure, athlete-exposure, match-exposure, or standalone rate dataset is reported in this award-summary publication.
recommendations.denominatorEvidenceQuote: Both groups were followed for one football season (August 2021–May 2022).
